historical_references.reference: Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded in their Sahih collections a Hadith narrated by Said ibn Al-Musayyab, who mentioned that during the Tabari Caliphate, 'Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz wrote to him that he was sending him an amount of gold for the maintenance of the poor and needy in Medina.
historical_references.context: Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz was a caliph who ruled over the Umayyad Empire in Damascus, while Said ibn Al-Musayyab was a prominent scholar in Medina. The Hadith describes a charitable act during the Tabari Caliphate.

historical_references.reference: Tabari is the name of the famous historian and scholar, Muhammad ibn Jarir Tabari (839-923 AD, 270-310 AH). He wrote one of the most influential works in Islamic history, 'Tarikh al-Rusul wa l-Muluk', commonly known as 'The History of Prophets and Kings'. This work covers the history of the world from the creation to the late 10th century AD, and is a comprehensive and important source for understanding the early history of Islam and the Islamic world.
historical_references.context: Muhammad ibn Jarir Tabari was a prominent scholar and historian, known for his comprehensive work on world history, 'Tarikh al-Rusul wa l-Muluk'. His work covers the history of the world from the creation to the late 10th century AD and is an important source for understanding the early history of Islam and the Islamic world.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Tabari' is commonly associated with the eponymous historian and geographer Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari (839-923 AD). His works, including 'The History of al-Tabari' and 'The Chronicler of the Arabs', are significant sources for Islamic history and continue to be widely referenced in academic circles. In the modern context, 'Tabari' is also used as a surname among the global Muslim community. Scholars and researchers in the fields of Islamic history and Middle Eastern studies frequently engage with 'Tabari's works on various platforms such as Academia.edu, ResearchGate, and Google Scholar.
